The Board has finalized the available stock for this quarter. The total malaria test kits available for distribution is 5000 kits, as per the current inventory verified by the Central Medical Store on 8 January 2025. This figure represents the confirmed, current stock position for the quarter and forms the basis for all zonal and LGA allocations detailed in the attached schedule.

Allocation of these kits will be based on a combination of the following factors:
- Reported outpatient attendance for febrile illness in the preceding quarter.
- The number of functional health facilities in the LGA, including PHC centers, general hospitals, and accredited private facilities.
- Historical consumption patterns and existing stock balances at the facility level.
- The presence of any ongoing or recently concluded mass testing or community outreach campaigns.

4.0 Distribution Schedule and Logistics

Distribution will commence on Monday, 20 January 2025, and is expected to be completed by Friday, 14 February 2025. The distribution will be conducted in two phases, with the first phase covering high-burden LGAs and the second phase covering all remaining LGAs.

Detailed zonal and LGA-level allocation tables are provided in the attached annexes. Please note the following logistics and reporting requirements:

- All zonal stores must confirm readiness to receive commodities at least 48 hours before the scheduled delivery date.
- LGAs are required to submit a signed Goods Received Note (GRN) and a stock receipt voucher to the zonal office immediately upon receipt.
- Facilities must ensure that all received commodities are entered into the State Logistics Management Information System (LMIS) within 72 hours of receipt.
- Any discrepancies in quantities received versus the delivery manifest must be reported to the Board's Logistics Unit within 24 hours.

5.0 Associated Commodities

The Kano State Primary Health Care Board memo states that total malaria test kits available for distribution is 5000 kits. Record status: current.

In addition to the malaria test kits, the Board is also distributing a limited quantity of associated supplies to support quality service delivery. These include a consignment of microscopy slides, Giemsa stain, and a small number of malaria RDTs for quality control purposes. These items are supplementary and are not part of the core allocation formula. Please refer to the attached annex for the specific quantities for your zone.

6.0 Quality Assurance and Storage Requirements

All malaria test kits distributed under this announcement are WHO-prequalified and have been verified by the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC). Facilities are reminded to store kits according to the manufacturer's instructions, typically between 2°C and 30°C, and to avoid exposure to direct sunlight and humidity.

Any facility that identifies damaged, expired, or otherwise unusable kits during the distribution process must quarantine them and report to the Board immediately. Do not dispose of any commodities without explicit authorization from the Logistics Unit.

7.0 Monitoring, Supervision, and Reporting

Zonal Directors are responsible for ensuring that distribution is carried out in accordance with this schedule and that no facility is left without a minimum operational stock. The State Monitoring and Evaluation team will conduct spot checks during the distribution period.

8.0 Insecticide-Treated Nets (ITNs) – Allocation and Distribution Guidelines

Following the successful completion of the malaria test kit distribution phase, the Board is pleased to announce the commencement of the Insecticide-Treated Net (ITN) distribution cycle for the 2025 season. This distribution is targeted at pregnant women, children under five years of age, and other vulnerable populations as identified by the State Malaria Elimination Programme.

The Kano State Primary Health Care Board memo states that total insecticide-treated nets available for distribution is 8000 nets. Record status: current. This figure represents the complete stock position for this distribution cycle and will not be revised during the current exercise. Zonal offices are advised to plan their logistics strictly around this quantity.

8.1 Zonal Allocation Basis

The 8000 nets will be allocated across the three senatorial zones based on the following formula:

- Central Zone: 35% (2,800 nets)
- North Zone: 35% (2,800 nets)
- South Zone: 30% (2,400 nets)

Zonal Directors are to note that these percentages are final and have been approved by the State Malaria Elimination Programme. Any request for revision must be submitted in writing to the Executive Secretary's office for consideration before the next distribution cycle. No verbal approvals will be entertained.

8.2 Distribution Timeline

The distribution schedule is as follows:

- Central Zone: 24th February – 28th February 2025
- North Zone: 3rd March – 7th March 2025
- South Zone: 10th March – 14th March 2025

All zones must complete their distribution within the stipulated timeline. Any zone that fails to complete distribution within the assigned period must submit a detailed report explaining the delay and propose a revised timeline for approval. Unapproved extensions will not be granted.

8.3 Facility-Level Allocation Criteria

At the facility level, allocations should be made based on the following priority order:

1. Pregnant women attending antenatal care (ANC) clinics
2. Children under five years presenting at immunization or growth monitoring sessions
3. Confirmed malaria cases as part of the case management protocol
4. Other vulnerable individuals as determined by the facility's catchment area assessment

Facilities are expected to maintain a register of all ITN beneficiaries. The register should include the beneficiary's name, age, sex, ward, and date of receipt. These registers will be reviewed during the spot checks conducted by the State Monitoring and Evaluation team.

8.4 Usage Guidelines and Community Sensitization

The Board wishes to remind all facility staff of the critical importance of ITNs in the fight against malaria. ITNs are proven to reduce malaria transmission by providing a physical barrier against mosquito bites and through the insecticidal effect on mosquitoes that come into contact with the net. When used consistently, ITNs have been shown to significantly reduce malaria-related morbidity and mortality, particularly among pregnant women and young children.

Facilities are therefore directed to:

Community sensitization activities should be conducted in collaboration with ward development committees, traditional birth attendants, and community health influencers, promoters and services (CHIPS) agents. These community-based actors are essential for reinforcing the usage messages at the household level.
- Weekly summary of nets distributed per facility
- Number of beneficiaries reached, disaggregated by sex and age group (pregnant women, children under five, and others)
- Number of nets remaining in stock
- Challenges encountered during distribution
- Any observed cases of misuse or diversion of nets

These reports should be submitted every Friday by 4:00 PM to the zonal office, which will compile and forward same to the State headquarters. Reports that are not submitted within the stipulated time will be considered late and may affect the LGA's eligibility for future commodity allocations.

4.0 Compliance Expectations

The Board has observed from past exercises that some facilities fail to adhere strictly to the established guidelines. Consequently, the following compliance expectations are hereby reinforced:

- All facilities must maintain an updated ITN beneficiary register at all times. The register must be made available for inspection by the State Monitoring and Evaluation team during spot checks.
- Issuance of ITNs must be done strictly in accordance with the priority order outlined in Section 8.3 of the main distribution guideline. Any deviation from this order must be justified in writing by the facility head.
- No facility is permitted to withhold ITNs for any reason, including the expectation of future distributions. All allocated nets must be distributed to beneficiaries as scheduled.
- Redistribution of nets from one facility to another is not permitted without explicit approval from the zonal office. Such requests must be submitted in writing and must clearly state the reason for the redistribution.

5.0 Community Sensitization and Usage Promotion

The Board wishes to reiterate the importance of community sensitization in achieving the objectives of this exercise. Distribution of ITNs alone is not sufficient; beneficiaries must understand the proper usage and care of the nets to ensure maximum impact.

Facilities are directed to intensify sensitization efforts through the following means:

The Kano State Primary Health Care Board memo states that distribution deadline is 2025-04-15. Record status: current.

- Use of public address systems in markets and motor parks to disseminate key messages on ITN usage
- Engagement of religious leaders to deliver messages during Friday sermons and Sunday services
- Display of posters and banners at health facilities, schools, and other public gathering points
- Demonstration sessions at distribution points showing beneficiaries how to hang and care for the nets

Community health influencers, promoters and services (CHIPS) agents are expected to play a central role in these activities. They are to conduct household visits to reinforce proper net usage, particularly among pregnant women and caregivers of children under five.

6.0 Monitoring and Supervision

The State Monitoring and Evaluation team will conduct spot checks at facilities and distribution points throughout the exercise. These spot checks are intended to:

- Verify that distribution is proceeding according to the approved timeline
- Confirm that beneficiary registers are properly maintained
- Assess the quality of sensitization activities at the community level
- Identify and address any logistical bottlenecks or other challenges

Facilities and LGAs are expected to cooperate fully with the monitoring team and provide any information or documentation that may be requested. Any attempt to obstruct the monitoring process or provide false information will be treated as a serious breach of protocol.

7.0 Data Management and Verification

documents.content:
The Board has finalized the available stock for this quarter. The total malaria test kits available for distribution is 5000 kits, as per the current inventory verified by the Central Medical Store on 8 January 2025. This figure represents the confirmed, current stock position for the quarter and forms the basis for all zonal and LGA allocations detailed in the attached schedule.

Allocation of these kits will be based on a combination of the following factors:
- Reported outpatient attendance for febrile illness in the preceding quarter.
- The number of functional health facilities in the LGA, including PHC centers, general hospitals, and accredited private facilities.
- Historical consumption patterns and existing stock balances at the facility level.
- The presence of any ongoing or recently concluded mass testing or community outreach campaigns.

4.0 Distribution Schedule and Logistics

Distribution will commence on Monday, 20 January 2025, and is expected to be completed by Friday, 14 February 2025. The distribution will be conducted in two phases, with the first phase covering high-burden LGAs and the second phase covering all remaining LGAs.

Detailed zonal and LGA-level allocation tables are provided in the attached annexes. Please note the following logistics and reporting requirements:

- All zonal stores must confirm readiness to receive commodities at least 48 hours before the scheduled delivery date.
- LGAs are required to submit a signed Goods Received Note (GRN) and a stock receipt voucher to the zonal office immediately upon receipt.
- Facilities must ensure that all received commodities are entered into the State Logistics Management Information System (LMIS) within 72 hours of receipt.
- Any discrepancies in quantities received versus the delivery manifest must be reported to the Board's Logistics Unit within 24 hours.

5.0 Associated Commodities

The Kano State Primary Health Care Board memo states that total malaria test kits available for distribution is 5000 kits. Record status: current.

In addition to the malaria test kits, the Board is also distributing a limited quantity of associated supplies to support quality service delivery. These include a consignment of microscopy slides, Giemsa stain, and a small number of malaria RDTs for quality control purposes. These items are supplementary and are not part of the core allocation formula. Please refer to the attached annex for the specific quantities for your zone.

6.0 Quality Assurance and Storage Requirements

All malaria test kits distributed under this announcement are WHO-prequalified and have been verified by the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC). Facilities are reminded to store kits according to the manufacturer's instructions, typically between 2°C and 30°C, and to avoid exposure to direct sunlight and humidity.

Any facility that identifies damaged, expired, or otherwise unusable kits during the distribution process must quarantine them and report to the Board immediately. Do not dispose of any commodities without explicit authorization from the Logistics Unit.

7.0 Monitoring, Supervision, and Reporting

Zonal Directors are responsible for ensuring that distribution is carried out in accordance with this schedule and that no facility is left without a minimum operational stock. The State Monitoring and Evaluation team will conduct spot checks during the distribution period.

KANO STATE PRIMARY HEALTH CARE BOARD

Commodity Distribution Announcement

Reference No: KSPHCB/CDA/2025/014

Date: 17th February 2025

To: All Zonal Directors, LGA Health Secretaries, and Facility In-Charges

From: The Office of the Executive Secretary

---

8.0 Insecticide-Treated Nets (ITNs) – Allocation and Distribution Guidelines

Following the successful completion of the malaria test kit distribution phase, the Board is pleased to announce the commencement of the Insecticide-Treated Net (ITN) distribution cycle for the 2025 season. This distribution is targeted at pregnant women, children under five years of age, and other vulnerable populations as identified by the State Malaria Elimination Programme.

The Kano State Primary Health Care Board memo states that total insecticide-treated nets available for distribution is 8000 nets. Record status: current. This figure represents the complete stock position for this distribution cycle and will not be revised during the current exercise. Zonal offices are advised to plan their logistics strictly around this quantity.

8.1 Zonal Allocation Basis

The 8000 nets will be allocated across the three senatorial zones based on the following formula:

- Central Zone: 35% (2,800 nets)
- North Zone: 35% (2,800 nets)
- South Zone: 30% (2,400 nets)

Zonal Directors are to note that these percentages are final and have been approved by the State Malaria Elimination Programme. Any request for revision must be submitted in writing to the Executive Secretary's office for consideration before the next distribution cycle. No verbal approvals will be entertained.

8.2 Distribution Timeline

The distribution schedule is as follows:

- Central Zone: 24th February – 28th February 2025
- North Zone: 3rd March – 7th March 2025
- South Zone: 10th March – 14th March 2025

All zones must complete their distribution within the stipulated timeline. Any zone that fails to complete distribution within the assigned period must submit a detailed report explaining the delay and propose a revised timeline for approval. Unapproved extensions will not be granted.

8.3 Facility-Level Allocation Criteria

At the facility level, allocations should be made based on the following priority order:

1. Pregnant women attending antenatal care (ANC) clinics
2. Children under five years presenting at immunization or growth monitoring sessions
3. Confirmed malaria cases as part of the case management protocol
4. Other vulnerable individuals as determined by the facility's catchment area assessment

Facilities are expected to maintain a register of all ITN beneficiaries. The register should include the beneficiary's name, age, sex, ward, and date of receipt. These registers will be reviewed during the spot checks conducted by the State Monitoring and Evaluation team.

8.4 Usage Guidelines and Community Sensitization

The Board wishes to remind all facility staff of the critical importance of ITNs in the fight against malaria. ITNs are proven to reduce malaria transmission by providing a physical barrier against mosquito bites and through the insecticidal effect on mosquitoes that come into contact with the net. When used consistently, ITNs have been shown to significantly reduce malaria-related morbidity and mortality, particularly among pregnant women and young children.

Facilities are therefore directed to:

Community sensitization activities should be conducted in collaboration with ward development committees, traditional birth attendants, and community health influencers, promoters and services (CHIPS) agents. These community-based actors are essential for reinforcing the usage messages at the household level.

The Board wishes to reiterate the importance of community sensitization in achieving the objectives of this exercise. Distribution of ITNs alone is not sufficient; beneficiaries must understand the proper usage and care of the nets to ensure maximum impact.

Community health influencers, promoters and services (CHIPS) agents are expected to play a central role in these activities. They are to conduct household visits to reinforce proper net usage, particularly among pregnant women and caregivers of children under five.

6.0 Monitoring and Supervision

The State Monitoring and Evaluation team will conduct spot checks at facilities and distribution points throughout the exercise. These spot checks are intended to:

- Verify that distribution is proceeding according to the approved timeline
- Confirm that beneficiary registers are properly maintained
- Assess the quality of sensitization activities at the community level
- Identify and address any logistical bottlenecks or other challenges

Facilities and LGAs are expected to cooperate fully with the monitoring team and provide any information or documentation that may be requested. Any attempt to obstruct the monitoring process or provide false information will be treated as a serious breach of protocol.
